summary: Practise hazard identification, risk scoring and workplace controls in a five-day occupational health and safety course. Explore the outline and enrol.
lede: Occupational health and safety training helps safety officers, supervisors and frontline team leads identify hazards and select practical controls for everyday work. You’ll practise job safety analysis and risk scoring, apply the hierarchy of controls, and record incidents and corrective actions, with additional work on safety data sheets and emergency response.
audienceIntro: This foundation course is designed for people who take part in everyday hazard control, safety coordination or incident response. It suits those who need practical ways to identify unsafe conditions and communicate actions across work teams.
modules: ILO-OSH Duties and Daily Safety Routines
Hierarchy of Controls in Routine Work
prerequisites: Expected preparation: familiarity with a workplace task or work area. No coding or specialist software skills are required; practical examples can use paper records or a spreadsheet.
